data.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?

result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\.

My overall pick is **1Password for ease of use and team collaboration**, while Bitwarden is the better choice if keeping costs down is a priority.

A team password manager should do more than store passwords. It should let you securely share credentials, control who can access them, and revoke access immediately when someone leaves.

## My top 4 recommendations

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password Business**

(Best overall)

- Excellent user experience.
- Shared vaults with granular permissions.
- Admin controls and security reporting.
- Great for non-technical teams.

Business: approximately US\$8.99/user/month. Teams Starter Pack: US\$24.95/month for 10 users.

[1Password business plans](https://1password.com/business)

---

![Free High-Quality Bitwarden Logo for Creative Design](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/p0IJzf2NCUQ2t02rqtPWDpe7Tx4YGCRNleASv1NjpztaDI--7OD-0zWJhdBi_4Wn4-v0Hr3hoS6JA2KXHdCOlvvdfHelZm6tTBmFuxgAbBftLkdqobRCpEkp4ysyI4Rm6vafJPMfHi8ri9Tdeng_QKXRw7C7a5ESA6hn8XLhRMLnvM7oFmwZESsO4_SFLJaX?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden Teams**

(Best value)

- Open-source password manager.
- Shared collections and team management.
- Audit and event logs.
- Good administrative controls for the price.

Approximately US\$4/user/month, billed annually.

[Bitwarden business plans](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Good admin and access controls.
- Shared folders and secure credential sharing.
- Strong option for businesses with more formal security requirements.

Business Starter advertised around US\$2/user/month; check plan limits.

[Keeper business plans](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![The best password managers in 2025 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/S30I88layvxbkaDwXaWP5XnJ7U511ARCXJEcDjYd8i8QoMbXMBiKKYXroCriJ7kBR0oi7lM-NLlyOXMHqaLP4YKGj6rWlLsTvfSS4pKj24h_up7wZjWKu6xYF8rT-_7bc8XbvU4PlaIDiwcj88cnT8GVhbZrDMRuBptQttvTl2oiFqpoAxV9-pe3un--FrSZ?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

- Privacy-focused approach.
- Secure sharing and team administration.
- Useful if your organisation already uses Proton products.

Worth comparing for budget-conscious, privacy-focused teams.

[Proton Pass for business](https://proton.me/business/pass)

## Quick comparison

| Feature | 1Password | Bitwarden | Keeper | Proton |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Ease of use | Excellent | Good | Very good | Very good |
| Team sharing | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent | Very good |
| Admin controls | Excellent | Very good | Excellent | Good |
| Budget friendly | Moderate | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent |
| Best for | General teams | Value | Security controls | Privacy |


Pricing is indicative in USD, generally on annual billing, and may vary by plan and Australian checkout. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[cybercred.com.au](https://cybercred.com.au/articles/password-managers-compared-for-small-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[velotouch.com](https://velotouch.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd look for before choosing

Whichever you choose, make sure it supports\:

1. **Shared vaults\:** Share accounts without sending passwords over Slack or email.
2. **Individual accounts\:** Every employee has their own login.
3. **Role-based permissions\:** Control who can view, edit and share credentials.
4. **Offboarding\:** Remove an employee's access immediately when they leave.
5. **2FA enforcement\:** Require two-factor authentication.
6. **Audit logs\:** Know who accessed or changed shared credentials.

## A couple of questions to narrow it down

I'd like to make a more specific recommendation rather than simply pick the most popular product.

**1\. How many people will use it?**
